main_text.p: maledictas. Et erit, si polluta fuerit, prævarica-catag; fuerit prævaricationem in virum suum: tunc ingredientur in eam aquæ maledictæ, versæ in amaritudinem, intumescetq; uterus ejus, & cadet femur ejus, & erit mulier illa in maledictionem in medio populi sui. Quòd si non fuerit polluta mulier, sed munda fuerit: munda erit, seminabitúrque semine, hoc est, fœcunda fiet, ex singulari Dei benedictione, quæ ipsi absolutionis erit sigillum. Num.s.v.12.

Si acceperit vir uxorem, & coierit cum ea, 23 accidat autem, ut non inveniat gratiam in oculis ejus, quòd invenerit in ea turpitudinem aliquam, & scripserit ei libellum repudii, ac posuerit in manu ejus, ejecerit q; eam è domo suâ: & egressa è domo illius abierit, ac nupserit viro alteri: & ille quoq; vir posterior odio habuerit illam, atque scripserit ei libellum repudii, posuerit q; in manu ejus, & ejecerit eâ è domo suâ; aut si mortuus fuerit vir ille posterior, qui acceperat eam uxorem: maritus ejus prior, qui ejecerat eam, iterum eam non accipito, ut sit ipsi uxor, posteaquam polluta est, ut maximè velit eam recipere. Deut.24 v.1.

page.notes: The left printed page is cut off at the scan edge; only fragments of its outer margin notes are visible, too short and cropped to read reliably, so they are not transcribed. A small mark (dot) stands before "ejus" in the left margin of the right page; it is not clearly a reference mark to a note. "Num.s.v.12." is printed with a long-s-like character after "Num."; read as s and marked for doubt in the reference. "praevaricatag;" is partly cut at the line end and the abbreviation is doubtful. Running head is given as printed on the right page (left and centre parts, both repeated at top). No catchword or signature is visible at the foot.
